subtopics.title: Development versus Growth — and How Development Is Measured

questions.question: A gas-exporting state posts a decade of rising GDP while half its children never finish primary school. This is best described as:
The HDI combines income per person, life expectancy at birth and:
South Africa holds an upper-middle income ranking but a noticeably lower HDI ranking. The gap between the two rankings represents:
options: Proof that the HDI ignores income
The development deficit — health and education lagging behind what our production predicts

questions.question: A family sits just above the food poverty line but lacks adequate schooling, sanitation, housing and work. The measure designed to capture their situation is:

subtopics.title: The Six Signs — Common Characteristics of Developing Countries

questions.question: The seamstress who cannot out-produce a factory because she has no machine, and cannot save for a machine because she earns so little, illustrates:
options: The vicious circle of low productivity

questions.question: A heavy dependency burden harms development mainly because:
options: Income needed for saving and investment is consumed by dependants' immediate needs
It lowers the population growth rate

questions.question: South Africa is called an extreme case on unemployment because:
options: The official rate is above thirty percent and the expanded rate above forty
Unemployment exists only in the informal sector
The rate is close to the world average

questions.question: South Africa's partial fit on primary-sector dependence has a precise shape:
options: Agriculture dominates both production and exports
Neither production nor exports involve minerals
Mining dominates production but not exports
Services dominate production, yet exports still lean on platinum, gold, coal and iron ore

subtopics.title: Development Strategies — and South Africa's Succession of Plans

questions.question: A country that walls off home industries behind tariffs so domestic manufacturing can grow up protected is following:
The emergency the RDP answered in 1994 was:
options: Communities deliberately starved of houses, water, electricity and clinics

questions.question: GEAR's bet, and its outcome, are correctly paired as:
options: Bet on tariffs; outcome was hyperinflation
Bet on grants; outcome was full employment
Bet on state ownership; outcome was privatisation
Bet that stable finances would draw job-creating investment; finances steadied but jobs lagged

questions.question: Which set correctly names delivery instruments running alongside the NDP 2030?
options: Expanded Public Works Programme, special economic zones, social grants
Import quotas, price ceilings, wage freezes
Currency controls, gold sales, land tax
Export bans, fuel subsidies, rent boards

subtopics.title: Indigenous Knowledge Systems — Development from Within

questions.question: Indigenous Knowledge Systems are transmitted mainly through:
Stokvels and burial societies together demonstrate that IKS can supply:
options: Core financial functions — savings mobilisation and insurance — built on trust

questions.question: The hoodia case is the standard illustration of biopiracy because:
options: The plant was smuggled out of the country
The San refused to share their knowledge
The patent was never used commercially
San knowledge was patented for profit without consent or payment

questions.question: The rooibos benefit-sharing outcome matters for development policy because it shows:
options: Indigenous knowledge is an asset that can earn recognised income for its holders
Traditional knowledge has no legal standing

subtopics.title: Taller or Better? — What Development Actually Asks

questions.question: In the analogy of the boy who grows ten centimetres, the pencil mark on the wall stands for:
options: Growth — the part that is easy to measure

questions.question: A mobile clinic, library computers and a bursary programme improve a town before payslips change. This shows:
South Africa's scorecard compressed to one line reads:
options: Richer than we are healthy or educated
Equal on money, health and learning

subtopics.title: The Six Signs, Walked Down One Street

questions.question: Coal trucks thundering to the port while the shop shelves hold only imported tools is the street version of:
options: Selling raw and buying made — primary export dependence

questions.question: One payslip and one pension supporting a household of eight illustrates:
The substation that trips, the fridge that dies and the loan the bank declines belong to which sign?
The 'sting in the tail' of the low standard of living scene is that:
options: A comfortable suburb sits minutes away — the gap matters as much as the average
Everyone on the street earns the same

subtopics.title: Plans on Paper, Roots in the Ground

questions.question: The three chapters of South Africa's planning story, in order, are:
The honest report card on the plans reads:
options: Growth targets met; services never delivered
Basics and the income floor largely delivered; growth and jobs repeatedly missed
Nothing was delivered on any front

questions.question: In a stokvel, the money a member carries home in their month comes from:
options: A bank loan taken by the group
The pooled monthly contributions of all the members, taken in turns

questions.question: Joining the plans and the roots means policy should:
options: Build products and programmes on trusted institutions — stokvel logic, healers, drought crops
Replace all indigenous institutions with formal ones
Patent community knowledge on behalf of the state
